name: a subprotocol both sides name is selected at the handshake, and a server naming one still takes a client that names none
description: What the handshake selected is what both peers report, and the profile is spoken over the connection either way: nothing about it turns on a subprotocol. The case a suite cannot hold is a client that offers meeting a server that selects none — a browser and Node's WebSocket refuse that handshake and Go's client takes it, so offering and selecting are one decision the two sides take together (docs/profile.md).

steps.note: the client offered one of the two the server names, so that one was selected
and the server reports the same token off the same handshake
a client that names none is met by a server that names some: none is selected, so a server may start naming subprotocols without breaking a client that never will
a peer refuses nothing on the ground that no subprotocol was negotiated
